title: Comfortably Numb
disambiguation: 6:49 album version, including "Is There Anybody Out There"
annotation:
The early 1980s CDs use this longer (6:49) edit which includes all of the "Time To Go", door knocks, and "Is There Anybody Out There" film bits left on the front of this track.  This leaves a shorter (0:51) [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/f4d42a74-cfb1-488d-a312-639034793cc1|Bring the Boys Back Home] in front of it on the CD

The shorter edit of [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/9ffabbe4-e078-4906-80a7-3a02b537e251|Comfortably Numb] is 6:24 and starts directly with the music leaving the film bits attached to the end of a longer (1:27) "[https://musicbrainz.org/recording/e7840a7d-38e4-4d69-b666-0ee4c92fe832|Bring the Boys Back Home]"

annotation:
This is the main, album, single, radio, and club version of "Hey Ya!". This version begins with André 3000 counting off immediately. The ending fadeout begins around the 3:36 mark. By 3:50 it's nearly inaudible. There are no censored words.

There is [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/4aa4434b-6dc9-4d2c-b5c5-c8361e6854d0|another version] with an extended outro, where the fadeout begins around the 3:46 mark and becomes inaudible around the 4:00 mark.

While nearly all "radio" and "clean" edits are this single/album version, there does exist a clean version which the phrase "cum-a" spoken at 2:01 is omitted: [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/b62be47d-c719-4bfe-a24c-d3569f2b4a9a|omits "cum-a"].

title: Insomnia
annotation:
AcoustID [https://acoustid.org/track/6f5c7822-15c6-4d2b-98b3-0101087b0c9a|6f5c7822-15c6-4d2b-98b3-0101087b0c9a] on original [https://musicbrainz.org/release/f1a882e4-637a-303e-b7eb-4eadd1b1fad1|Reverence] album.

''Different to the more commonly known [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/22679a0a-da3a-4cf6-b1a7-58ad97fdee8f|Monster Mix], but shares the same length so easy to confuse.''

Note the 8:40 version and 8:47 version.  The longer one has 7 seconds of the previous track on it.  This seems to be on the later re-releases of the album.  8:40 starts with the bells.

Checked from copies in hand...
